text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mahathir, the First Malaysian Prime Minister to visit Lebanon, proposes new concept for peace.

- Acting Finance Minister Siniora says Lebanese should learn from Malaysia's experience about rehabilitation of economic growth, privatisation, slashing number of public sector employees and limiting inflation.
- Lebanon demands the extradition of fugitive businessman and banker Roger Tamraz.
- Israel's south Lebanon shelling causes fires in central and eastern sectors.
- Most ministers want the government to reconsider the ban on the import of foods that can be grown in Lebanon.
- Some Lebanese insist on staying in Freetown and Brazzaville despite troubles.
- Prosecutor charges 23 customs agents and emloyees with forgery and bribery.
- Trial of Red Army guerrillas resumes on July 7.
- Weekly treasury bill auction registers new surplus of subscription against maturity.
